# Code Review Practices for AI-Generated Code

This dimension covers how code review should adapt when code is AI-generated.

## Review Rounds and Effort

Humans require more effort to review AI-generated code than human-written code [11]:
- **11.8% more review rounds** when reviewing AI code vs. human code
- 85-87% of AI-initiated reviews ended after first comment (superficial engagement)
- Understanding feedback triggered 2.1-2.3 discussion rounds average

## AI Suggestion Adoption Gap

AI code review suggestions are adopted at dramatically lower rates than human suggestions [11]:
- AI suggestion adoption rate: **16.6%**
- Human suggestion adoption rate: **56.5%**
- Gap: 39.9 percentage points

Why AI suggestions are rejected (383-sample analysis) [11]:
- 28.7% marked as incorrect
- 24.0% addressed through alternative developer fixes
- Remaining: unnecessary, deferred, or style preferences

## Issue Density in AI-Generated Code

AI PRs contain substantially more issues across all categories [7]:

| Category | AI vs Human Multiplier |
|----------|----------------------|
| Overall issues/PR | 1.7x (10.83 vs 6.45) |
| Security | up to 2.74x |
| Logic/correctness | 1.75x |
| Readability | 3x |
| Error handling | ~2x |
| Excessive I/O | ~8x |
| Formatting | 2.66x |
| Naming inconsistencies | ~2x |

Sample: 470 PRs (320 AI co-authored, 150 human-only) [7].

## Review Fatigue and Automation Complacency

From [14] (aggregating multiple studies):
- Performance declines after **30 minutes** of sustained monitoring
- Under reliable automation, operators detect only **~30% of errors**
- When system shows visible failures, detection jumps to **~75%**
- Security analysts receive 4,484 alerts daily; 67% go uninvestigated; 83% are false positives
- AI-assisted developers wrote less secure code but believed it more secure
- Task inexperience: 26% higher rate of following erroneous automated advice

**Recommended mitigations** [14]:
- Mandatory breaks every 2 hours minimum
- 25-30 minute focused review intervals
- Pair programming for high-risk reviews
- Smaller PR units for AI-generated code

## AI Comment Verbosity

AI reviewers are significantly more verbose [11]:
- AI: 29.6 tokens per line of code
- Human: 4.1 tokens per line of code (~7.2x more verbose)
- 95%+ of AI comments focused on improvement and defect detection

This verbosity may contribute to review fatigue — more text to process without proportionally more value.

## Scale Deployments

| Organization | Scale | Key Metric |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Copilot | 60M cumulative reviews [12] | 71% actionable feedback |
| Microsoft | 600K+ PRs/month [13] | 90% PR coverage |
| GitHub ecosystem | 1 in 5 reviews use Copilot [12] | 12,000+ orgs |

Microsoft reports 10-20% median PR completion time improvement with AI review [13].

## Code Quality Impact of AI Suggestions

Adopted AI suggestions increased code complexity [11]:
- AI suggestions: increased cyclomatic complexity by 0.085-0.106
- Human suggestions: -0.002 to 0.009 (essentially neutral)
- AI added 0.216 statements vs. human 0.108

This suggests AI suggestions tend to add code rather than simplify, potentially making codebases harder to maintain.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Most large-scale quantitative data comes from vendor/first-party sources (GitHub, Microsoft, CodeRabbit)
- No independent academic study at enterprise scale
- Limited data on how reviewer expertise affects ability to catch AI code issues
- No controlled experiments comparing different review approaches (checklists, pair review, AI-assisted)
- Review fatigue data drawn from non-software domains (radiology, security monitoring)
- Unknown what percentage of AI code issues are caught in review vs. escaping to production
